On 28 May 2024, the resident raised a complaint stating she reported mould in October 2023, the landlord completed a mould spray treatment but the mould came back, she was pregnant and the mould was affecting her and her 1-year-old son's health, mould in kitchen, bedrooms, toilet and living room damaged wallpaper and personal belongings. partial_case.facts: The resident lived in a 2-bedroom flat with her partner and 2 young children. She reported mould to the landlord on 16 October 2023 and said delay in addressing it affected her and her children’s health and damaged belongings. The complaint concerned the landlord’s handling of mould reports and compensation for mould damage, and its handling of the complaint. On 28 May 2024 the resident complained that mould reported in October 2023 had returned, that she was pregnant, that mould affected her and her 1-year-old son’s health, and that mould in the kitchen, bedrooms, toilet and living room damaged wallpaper and personal belongings. The landlord’s stage 1 response said a damp and mould survey had been completed on 7 December 2023 and a mould treatment on 9 April 2024. At stage 2 the landlord offered £300 compensation for failure to progress stage 1 actions; on 30 January 2025 it offered a further £1000 for delay, distress and inconvenience; and on 10 February 2025 it told its insurer to consider compensation for mould-damaged items. The resident later asked the Ombudsman to investigate because she said the compensation did not cover mould-damaged items, redecoration, distress, hospital time with children ill from mould exposure, or the cavity wall repairs she wanted completed.

The landlord’s complaint responses were timely and in line with its complaint policy response times.
Overall, the landlord took over 14 months to complete the relevant mould works.
The compensation was proportionate redress for the prolonged delay in resolving the mould issues and lack of regard for vulnerabilities.
It is therefore our view that the landlord has provided the resident reasonable redress for the failings identified.
